payload.title: Hand a step back with a reason; a person takes a step over
payload.description:
Two record changes cover hand-back and take-over. An agent that finds a problem in an earlier step reopens that checklist step with a reason; the change wakes the step's agent. A person takes a step over by assigning it to themselves; agents then stand down on that step until it is released or closed. Both use the existing checklist sub-task Items, and both are recorded with actor and reason.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A reopened step runs its agent again with the reason in its input.
- An agent never works a step a person has taken.
- Releasing the step lets the agent resume.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- step-handback.feature: the copy editor reopens fact-check with a reason; the fact-checker runs with that reason; a person takes a step and the agent stands down; release resumes it.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Work items and handoffs between agents and people. Slice code F2 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
